moa.t: Blocks carbonic anhydrase in the proximal tubule and choroid plexus: bicarbonate diuresis, reduced CSF and aqueous production

dosing_note: Doses are extracted automatically from the guideline text. Each heading is the nearest section title in the guideline and can be off by one section – confirm on the cited page. The pathway dose stays authoritative for its indication.

items.t: Acetazolamide, oral, 250 mg 12 hourly · Increase, as required, by 250 mg daily every week to the maximum tolerated dose (not exceeding 4 g daily).
Acetazolamide, oral, 500 mg immediately as a single dose. · Followed by 250 mg 6 hourly.
Acetazolamide, oral, 500 mg, immediately, followed by 250 mg 6 hourly until referred.
Acetazolamide, oral, 20 mg/kg/dose 8 hourly. · Maximum daily dose: 1000 mg. · Monitor for metabolic acidosis and serum potassium derangements.

dosing.h: Supportive care for children with TBM

items.t: Acetazolamide (50 mg/kg/day) 6-hourly per os (maximum 2 grams per day). • This has been shown to normalise the intracranial pressure within seven days in most children, but not all. The duration of diuretic therapy is one month.

adverse_effects.t: Paraesthesiae, metabolic acidosis, hypokalaemia, renal stones, fatigue, taste disturbance
